thread:
incidents-bot: [P0 PAGE] batcher-accumulator node flapping detected in pool-batcher-us-west-2. Symptoms: continuous-batcher queue growth, sudden GPU page faults, multiple container restarts. Routes affected: /v1/generate (high latency). Automated mitigations attempted: node drain, restart failed. Paging metric > 85% of capacity.

maya (oncall): I'm paged, jumping in. Observed 3 nodes with > 70% pagefaults and batcher accumulator count steadily climbing.

kevin (eng-runtime): logs show repeated CUDA page faults + OOM traces from the continuous-batcher process. Looks like accumulator size grows past threshold and triggers kernel faults. Sample log:```
[2026-03-15T02:05:12Z] batcher: accumulator.size=18446744073709551615
[2026-03-15T02:05:12Z] runtime: cuda error: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at kernel launch
[2026-03-15T02:05:13Z] runtime: out-of-memory trying to allocate 512MB for KV cache
```

maya (oncall): copying logs to thread. Immediate customer impact?

pranav (eng-infra): Cloud metrics show tail latency on /v1/generate spiking to 25s for 12m, and ~2% requests returning 500/503/429 due to queue overflow. Two paying customers reported errors via support.

maya (oncall): Mitigation plan proposed: (1) disable continuous batching on pool-batcher-us-west-2 to force per-request paths, (2) scale up fallback pool-batcher-fallback-small by +3 nodes, (3) drain offending nodes, (4) roll restart batcher service once config flagged. Anyone see reason not to?

kevin (eng-runtime): Agree. Also suggest reducing batch size limit and temporarily disable KV cache prefetch to avoid large allocations. Will push a config toggle.

maya (oncall): Doing steps now. Executing safe commands:```
# toggle continuous batching off for pool-batcher-us-west-2
redwoodctl config set pool-batcher-us-west-2.continuous_batching false --env prod
# scale fallback pool
kubectl -n runtime scale deployment/batcher-fallback-small --replicas=6
```

ops-bot: Command accepted. Change requests queued and applied by deploybot.

kevin (eng-runtime): Patching runtime config: lowering max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 1024 and disabling prefetch. Pushing canary to two nodes.

carla (sre): Noted. Initiating node drains on the three highest-error nodes to trigger handoff. If drain fails, we'll cordon and restart VM.

maya (oncall): After toggles: request latency falling back to ~800ms on fallback pool. Error rate dropping. Continuous-batcher metrics show accumulator shrink; no new CUDA page faults in last 90s.

pranav (eng-infra): One node failed to drain cleanly; kubelet reported container restart loop. I've force-restarted container runtime and rebooted host. Monitoring.

kevin (eng-runtime): Observed a secondary issue: a deadlock in the accumulator flush loop when a sudden mix of short/long sequences arrives. This triggers batch growth that bypasses queue backpressure. Need follow-up fix in runtime: add stronger backpressure and a bounded accumulator. Filing a ticket.

maya (oncall): Handing off to carla for night coverage. Summary so far: paging + CUDA pagefaults caused by continuous-batcher accumulator runaway. Immediate mitigation: disabled continuous batching in affected pool, scaled fallback, drained/flipped 3 nodes, rebooted one host. Latency and error rates recovering.

carla (sre): Taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring and will coordinate a controlled rollback of continuous batching only after we have a runtime fix. Can you post the customer impact details and contact list?

maya (oncall): Customers impacted: 2 enterprise tenants saw 500s/429s briefly (support tickets #4621, #4622). Internal alerting triggered SLO degradation for generate route: 12m window breached. No data loss reported.

pranav (eng-infra): Added temporary routing rule to prefer fallback pool for the two tenant IDs to reduce exposure while we investigate root cause.

kevin (eng-runtime): Created ticket RUNTIME-2345: "Accumulator drift -> batch growth -> kernel pagefaults". Patch plan: add accumulator caps, introduce periodic flush checks, and validate batch size heuristics against mixed sequence lengths. Post-deploy smoke-run with synthetic workload.

maya (oncall): Action items:
- kevin: deliver patch PR and coordinate canary (RUNTIME-2345).
- pr anav: keep fallback pool scaled + routing rule for affected tenants.
- carla: monitor overnight, escalate if paging recurs.
- maya: draft incident summary for ops and support.

carla (sre): Acknowledged. I'll run a short disruption test after hours to ensure restart/cordon sequence is reliable.

maya (oncall): Thanks all. Leaving channel. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: [UPDATE] incident acknowledged by carla (sre). Severity P0 -> Mitigated (partial).

carla (sre): Quick note for later postmortem: attach the sequence profiles that cause accumulator growth (mix of 32-token + 8k-token requests) and the exact kernel stack traces for the CUDA_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS. Also include the rollout window when we disabled continuous batching and the times we scaled fallback pool.

kevin (eng-runtime): Will attach logs and a minimal reproducer to RUNTIME-2345. Early repro uses a mix of short chat completions interleaved with long context embeddings causing batching misalignment.

carla (sre): Closing handoff — monitoring remains open. If paging reappears, escalate to infra pager.
